extracted.intended_audience: ICCV 2023 reviewers / peer reviewers in computer vision
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for reviewers assessing ICCV conference paper submissions, focusing on writing thorough, specific, anonymized, and constructive reviews that fairly evaluate novelty, scope, and guideline compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Take adequate time / thoughtful review
rubrics_metrics.description: Take the time to write good reviews. Ideally, you should read a paper and then think about it over the course of several days before you write your review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short reviews are unhelpful to authors, other reviewers, and Area Chairs. If you have agreed to review a paper, you should take enough time to write a thoughtful and detailed review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid short, superficial reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Short reviews are unhelpful to authors, other reviewers, and Area Chairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide thoughtful, detailed feedback rather than single-line judgments; explain reasoning so Area Chairs and other reviewers can act on it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be specific when suggesting writing improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: Be specific when you suggest that the writing needs to be improved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If there is a particular section that is unclear, point it out and give suggestions for how it can be clarified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be specific and evidence-based about novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: Be specific about novelty. Claims in a review that the submitted work 'has been done before' MUST be backed up with specific references and an explanation of how closely they are related.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For a positive review, summarize what novel aspects are most interesting in the Strengths section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not reject solely for missing citations to non-peer-reviewed prior work
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not reject papers solely because they are missing citations or comparisons to prior work that has only been published without review (e.g., arXiv or technical reports).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the FAQ for more details on handling arXiv prior art; absence of citation to non-peer-reviewed material is not by itself a reason for rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect author anonymity / avoid revealing identity
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't give away your identity by asking the authors to cite several of your own papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid requests or comments that would reveal the reviewer; maintain anonymization both in content requests and in phrasing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handle scope concerns clearly but keep an open mind
rubrics_metrics.description: If you think the paper is out of scope for ICCV's subject areas, clearly explain why in the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Then suggest other publication possibilities (journals, conferences, workshops) that would be a better match for the paper. However, unless area mismatch is extreme, you should keep an open mind, because we want a diverse set of good papers at the conference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain constructive, professional tone
rubrics_metrics.description: The tone of your review is important. A harshly written review will be resented by the authors, regardless of whether your criticisms are true.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is possible to word your review constructively while staying true to your thoughts. Avoid referring to the authors in the second person ('you'); use third person ('the authors' or 'the paper') to prevent confrontational tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide constructive suggestions for improvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Be generous about giving the authors new ideas for how they can improve their work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You might suggest a new technical tool that could help, a dataset that could be tried, an application area that might benefit from their work, or a way to generalize their idea to increase its impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not use guideline violations as an excuse for perfunctory rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Although author-guidelines list anonymization, template, length, and code requirements, reviewers should not instantly reject papers based solely on such violations in their review text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PCs have already filtered obvious violation cases. If you think a paper violates guidelines and should be rejected without review, email Program Chairs for instructions instead of writing a single-line review such as 'The paper violates a guideline and should be rejected'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not reject solely because of similar arXiv papers; report plagiarism concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers SHOULD NOT reject a paper solely because another paper with a similar idea has already appeared on arXiv.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the reviewer suspects plagiarism or academic dishonesty, bring these concerns to the attention of Area and Program Chairs rather than using arXiv prior appearance as an automatic rejection reason.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize that thoughtful reviews also benefit the reviewer
rubrics_metrics.description: A thoughtful review not only benefits the authors, but also yourself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Your reviews are read by other reviewers and especially the Area Chairs; being a helpful reviewer will generate goodwill in the research community and may help you to win an Outstanding Reviewer award.
